sources.title: Points and vertices
claimsUsed: A vertex references a point and primitives use vertices to reference points.
Primitives can share points while vertices remain unique to a primitive.
Coincident positions do not imply the same point-sharing topology.

sources.title: Geometry attributes
claimsUsed: Attributes can be owned by vertices, points, primitives or the whole detail.
Owner precedence and storage precision affect interpretation.
The conventional id attribute is distinct from element number and can track elements when numbering changes.

sources.title: Groups
claimsUsed: Ordered and unordered groups carry different ordering semantics.

sources.title: Primitives
claimsUsed: Polygons are defined by ordered vertex sequences.
Different primitive representations may have different attribute and topology semantics.

sources.title: hou.Geometry
claimsUsed: HOM exposes point, vertex, primitive and detail attribute sets separately.
HOM exposes point, primitive, edge and vertex groups separately.
Topology and primitive-intrinsic data IDs are change indicators, while the modification counter is not unique across geometry objects.

sources.title: hou.Attrib
claimsUsed: Attribute identity includes owner, data type, numeric precision, component size and qualifier metadata.

sources.title: Speed vs. reproducibility in Math Kernel Library
claimsUsed: Floating-point output may vary across runtimes, optimized paths, threading, alignment, hardware and control settings.
Reproducibility controls improve but do not universally guarantee identical output.

independence: One official SideFX documentation lineage plus a synthetic CPU fixture. Documentation authority and CI replay do not create independent Houdini runtime evidence.
